findings.impact: A release can pass its member completion gate while the isolated patch branch omits a supposedly completed fix.
findings.text: Enforce the requirement that an inserted patch line exists and is correctly based before any of its members can start or merge, and detect/recover members already completed on integration. Today target_of routes members without an open line to integration; merely specifying that the line should be created first does not stop a scheduler from completing a member on integration before line creation. Add a real remote fixture covering retarget/creation versus worker dispatch and completion.

findings.impact: An approved patch line can be created from an obsolete production commit after production advances, defeating the design’s baseline check and risking an incomplete or incorrectly based release.
findings.text: Specify an atomic or otherwise race-safe guard binding inserted-line creation to the owner-approved production source, including direct remote production advances between preflight and branch creation; internal line leases alone do not serialize external pushes. Prevent member work from using a stale line and test the actual remote race.

output.summary: Both prior release-isolation findings are resolved; no new material findings.
Approved G1051 design for arbitrarily nested numeric release targets, equivalent trailing-zero aliases, and safely isolated patch and maintenance releases.

responses.adversary_design:1:1: fixed: require verified isolated line and gate member dispatch, base and integration; detect already-completed members and preserve them for explicit reviewed backport.
responses.adversary_design:1:2: fixed: bind the line to an approved immutable source, recheck after conditional ref creation before member work, and enforce atomic expected-target checks at production promotion with explicit stale-source handling.
responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: require isolated baseline and member routing also when later work is uncut but has reached integration.
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: define inserted-line graph mode with record-only pre-approval line_sync and authorized post-finish propagation.
responses.review_design:1:3: fixed: recorded as owner decision Q1

output.summary: Use canonical arbitrarily nested release IDs and explicitly isolated patch lines that are verified before member work, including when later work is only planned. Bind creation to approved immutable source provenance, protect production promotion with atomic target checks, and keep older maintenance releases separate from newer production.

Both independent re-reviews resolved all prior findings. The revised design specifies pre-dispatch patch isolation, guarded line creation and forwarding, and the owner’s maintenance-release decision. No open findings or non-material notes remain to filter.

findings.impact: A patch can release unrelated later-version changes despite meeting all current release gates.
findings.text: The isolation path is specified only when a later release line already exists. If a later release is planned but uncut, some of its closed goals can already be merged into integration: current target_of() routes ordinary members to integration when no release line is open, and ordinary release cut starts from the integration tip. A newly inserted 2.1 can therefore include completed release-3 work even though 3 has not yet been cut. Define how an inserted target gets its verified released baseline and isolated member branch before its work merges in this case too, and test a later uncut target with later-only work already on integration.

findings.impact: Reusing the existing numbered release graph as described can publish unapproved patch code to integration before the finish decision and change other release cuts.
findings.text: The design promises patch changes are forwarded to integration only after finishing the patch, but the shipped release graph invokes git.line_sync before approve_finish and the current sync() immediately merges every release line into integration; only hotfix lines are record-only. Specify the inserted-line mode and changes to the release graph/line_sync that make pre-approval sync record the exact patch tip without integrating it, and test that neither integration nor other release branches receive the patch before the stated gate.

findings.impact: The design may reject exactly the old-release patch the owner expects, or an implementation that removes the guard could deliver the older baseline to the wrong production line.
findings.text: owner question: The owner asked that releases can always be inserted at deeper positions, but the proposed implementation refuses when production has already advanced past the desired released baseline and always finishes a patch by merging it to production. If release 3 is already in production, should an inserted 2.1 remain possible as a maintenance release on its own line (without moving the main production branch backwards), or should such targets be refused? Recommend supporting an isolated maintenance line while explicitly preventing an older patch from being merged into newer production automatically; if maintenance releases are out of scope, record that limitation as an owner decision.

not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.
intent.serves: Developers who delegate project work to coding agents, and the agents doing it.

output.summary: The revised design resolves all prior findings: it isolates inserted work before member dispatch, records patch heads without pre-approval forwarding, and implements the owner’s maintenance-release decision.

spec:
Support inserting a release between existing ZzzOps target releases, so a patch release can be planned and delivered without renumbering later work. The motivating example is targeting a patch release such as 2.1; target releases must no longer be restricted to integers. This is useful for shipping a ZzzOps fix as a patch while later releases are already planned.

Acceptance criteria:
- Let an owner insert, target and work toward an appropriately ordered release such as 2.1 alongside existing integer releases. Existing goals assigned to later releases remain assigned to those releases unless explicitly changed. A patch release can use the existing release workflow and gates.
- Define and validate release identifiers and their ordering explicitly. Avoid treating version-like identifiers as floating-point numbers: for example, 2.10 and 2.1 must not silently collapse into the same identifier. The supported identifier grammar and how it relates to actual semantic versions are design choices to surface to the owner if not already decided.
- Integrate the identifier through the actual engine, goal schema, CLI, default workflow, release and branch handling, scheduling, display, validation, docs and compatibility boundaries wherever relevant. Do not assume a particular release-branch naming scheme without checking existing policy.
- Preserve existing integer release data and goal histories; do not silently reorder, rewrite or repurpose existing releases or production branches. Analyze how existing repositories and in-flight goals adopt the new version; report unrelated broken migrations for a separate goal rather than expanding scope to repair them.
- Cover identifier parsing and ordering, insertion with later targets already present, scheduling, release cutting and completion, compatibility with existing integer goals, invalid and ambiguous input, branch/CLI behavior and mixed engine versions using realistic local Git/remote fixtures. Run focused real-engine checks first, followed by appropriate integration checks.

Constraints: ZzzOps release support is a branching strategy, not an automatic deployment or package-publishing service. Respect existing owner approvals and policy choices. Do not create a real release, change production branches, publish artifacts or change other goals' release assignments as part of capturing this goal.

Owner clarification: releases can always be inserted by adding another dot-delimited numeric component. For example, after 2.1 exists, insert 2.0.1 before it, then insert 2.0.0.1 before 2.0.1: 2 < 2.0.0.1 < 2.0.1 < 2.1. Support arbitrarily nested finite component sequences rather than imposing a fixed version depth. Trailing-zero forms representing the same value, such as 2 and 2.0, are equivalent; 2.1 and 2.10 remain distinct. Design and test ordering, canonical identity, branch naming, insertion, compatibility and safe patch-line ancestry at nested depths.
title: Allow inserting patch target releases between planned releases
